# Poisson Design

## Poisson design

The Poisson design is a generalization of the Bernoulli design (BE).

There are different inclusion probabilities $\pi_i\ \forall i \in U$.

We generate $N$ independent random numbers $U(0,1)$, $RN_1,\dots,RN_i,\dots,RN_N$.

If $RN_i<\pi_i$ individual $i$ is selected.

The sampling design is:

$$
p(s)=\prod\limits_{i \in s}\pi_i\prod\limits_{i \in U-s}(1-\pi_i)
$$

And the sample size $n_s$ is random, with

$$
E_{PO}(n_s)=\sum\limits_{i \in U}\pi_i \quad\text{and}\quad V_{PO}(n_s)=\sum\limits_{i \in U}\pi_i(1-\pi_i)
$$

## HT estimator under a PO design

Under the PO design the HT estimator of $Y=\sum\nolimits_{i\in U}y_i$ is:

$$
\hat{Y}_{\text{HT}}=\sum\limits_{i \in s}\frac{y_i}{\pi_i}
$$

Since the $I_i$ are independent, $\Delta_{ij}=0\ \forall\,i\neq j$. The variance of $\hat{Y}_{\text{HT}}$ is:

$$
V_{PO}(\hat{Y}_{\text{HT}})=\sum\limits_{i\in U}\left(\frac{1}{\pi_i}-1\right)y_i^2
$$

An unbiased estimator of $V_{PO}(\hat{Y}_{\text{HT}})$ is:

$$
\hat{V}_{PO}(\hat{Y}_{\text{HT}})=\sum\limits_{i \in s}\left(1-\pi_i\right)\frac{y_i^2}{\pi_i^2}
$$

# Choosing the $\pi_i$

## How do we choose the $\pi_i$?

So as to minimize $V_{PO}(\hat{Y}_{\text{HT}})$ and considering a fixed expected sample size $n$. That is:

$$ \min_{\pi_i}\ \sum\limits_{i\in U}\left(\frac{1}{\pi_i}-1\right)y_i^2 \quad\text{s.t.}\quad n=\sum\limits_{i \in U}\pi_i$$

Since

$$
\sum\limits_{i\in U}\left(\frac{1}{\pi_i}-1\right)y_i^2=\sum\limits_{i\in U}\frac{y_i^2}{\pi_i}-\sum\limits_{i \in U}y_i^2
$$

and $n$ is a constant, the problem above is equivalent to minimizing in $\pi_i$ the product

$$
\left(\sum\limits_{i \in U}\frac{y_i^2}{\pi_i}\right)\left(\sum\limits_{i\in U}\pi_i\right)
$$

## Choosing the $\pi_i$

::: {.block}
::: {.block-title}
Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
:::
$$
\left(\sum\nolimits_{i\in U}x_iz_i\right)^2\leq\left(\sum\limits_{i\in U}x_i^2\right)\left(\sum\limits_{i \in U}z_i^2\right)
$$
Equality holds if and only if $x_i=\lambda z_i$.
:::

Applying the inequality to the previous problem, we obtain:

$$
\left(\sum\limits_{i \in U}\left(\frac{y_i}{\sqrt{\pi_i}}\right)^2\right)\left(\sum\limits_{i\in U}\left(\sqrt{\pi_i}\right)^2\right)\geq\left(\sum\limits_{i \in U}\frac{y_i}{\sqrt{\pi_i}}\sqrt{\pi_i}\right)^2
$$

The minimum is reached at equality, which holds when

$$
\frac{y_i}{\sqrt{\pi_i}}=\lambda\sqrt{\pi_i}\quad\text{i.e. when}\quad\frac{y_i}{\pi_i}=\lambda
$$

## Choosing the $\pi_i$

Assume $y_i>0 \ \forall i$.

We have $\pi_i=\frac{y_i}{\lambda}$.

Then

$$n=\sum\nolimits_{i\in U}\pi_i=\sum\limits_{i \in U}\frac{y_i}{\lambda}=\frac{Y}{\lambda}$$

Substituting $\lambda$ we obtain:

$$\pi_i=n\frac{y_i}{\sum\limits_{i\in U}y_i}$$

## Choosing the $\pi_i$

It happens that $y$ is unknown, but we may have a variable $x$, known for all of $U$ and possibly correlated with variable $y$. In that case the inclusion probabilities are determined by:

$$\pi_i=n\frac{x_i}{\sum\limits_{i \in U}x_i} $$

These designs are called **probability proportional to size** and the value of $x_i$ is the "measure of size" (MOS) of individual $i$.

If $\frac{y_i}{x_i}\doteq c$ the estimator will have a small variance.

## Conclusions on the PO design

The PO design is a generalization of the BE design, so it also has a random sample size. Suppose for a moment that the values of $y$ are known and the initial $\pi_i$ can be computed. In this case

$$
\hat Y_{\text{HT}}=\frac{n_s}{n}Y
$$

The only source of randomness is the sample size $n_s$.

Can a probability-proportional-to-size design of fixed size be implemented?
